# CodeVault

> CodeVault is an open-source (MIT), syntax-aware code snippet library for developers. Store, organize, search, and reuse the code you write: a Monaco-powered editor, flat #tags, private-by-default snippets, full-text search, and one-click copy — in the browser, plus Chrome and VS Code extensions. Free to use, free to self-host.

CodeVault is free with no paid tiers. Anyone can browse public snippets; an account (Google or GitHub sign-in) is only needed to create and manage your own.

## Product

- [Homepage](https://codevault-olive.vercel.app/): features, live demo, testimonials, and FAQ
- [Sign in](https://codevault-olive.vercel.app/auth): create an account with Google or GitHub
- [REST API](https://github.com/Anos714/CodeVault/blob/main/docs/api.md): PAT-authenticated `/api/v1` endpoints for snippets, tokens, and profile

## Extensions

- [Chrome extension](https://github.com/Anos714/CodeVault/tree/main/chrome-extension): save code selections from any web page into your vault
- [VS Code extension](https://github.com/Anos714/CodeVault/tree/main/vscode-extension): insert snippets from your vault at the cursor

## Features

- Monaco editor: the same engine that powers VS Code — real syntax highlighting, indentation, and instant language switching
- Search: match on title, language, description, or tags, with a ⌘K command palette
- Tags: flat #tags instead of deep folders
- Privacy: every snippet is private by default; one switch makes it public and shareable
- Copy: one-click copy to clipboard, or insert straight into Chrome and VS Code
- Themes: light and dark, both tuned for long reading sessions
- Sharing: unlisted share links and embeddable iframes for READMEs and Notion

## How it works

1. Capture: paste or write a snippet in the Monaco editor with a title, a note, and a language
2. Organize: tag it (#auth, #regex), keep it private or mark it public
3. Reuse: search by title, language, or tag and copy in one click — or insert it in Chrome and VS Code

## FAQ

- Is CodeVault free? Yes — open source under the MIT license; self-host it or use the hosted version at no cost.
- Do I need an account to browse public snippets? No. Anyone can browse public snippets; an account is only required to create and manage your own.
- Which languages are supported? Anything you can type — popular languages highlight out of the box, and Monaco handles dozens more.
- Can I keep snippets private? Yes — every snippet defaults to private, with one switch to share it publicly.
- Is my data portable? Yes — copy any snippet in one click, and the source is fully open if you would rather self-host.
